outcomes: Each Rush project is a Putnami project with an edge to each Rush project its package.json depends on, in the mode the workspace adopted
In delegate mode, putnami build, test and lint run rush on each affected project, and Rush's build cache decides what reruns
In import mode, each Rush project is a TypeScript project that Putnami's runner, installer and cache serve
nonGoals: Installing or switching a Rush version: the toolchain check compares and never installs
Rewriting rush.json or command-line.json, or a project's package.json beyond the exports an import adds (D-066)
Rush subspaces, version policies and publishing: rush publish and rush version keep running through Rush
A Rush repository whose rush.json is not at the Putnami workspace root

requirements.text: In delegate mode, the probe answers each rush.json project: its folder, its packageName as source name and as the name rush receives, the projects the putnami observe Rush detector says it depends on, the extension @putnami/rush, the tag rush and the workspace root as stack root. In import mode, set in options.@putnami/rush.mode of putnami.workspace.json, it answers no project, so the TypeScript extension runs them.

The workspace sync task reads rush.json and each project's package.json and writes in each project's putnami.json the extension of the mode, @putnami/rush or @putnami/typescript, and the project IDs it depends on. In delegate mode it adds rush.json and common/config/rush/command-line.json as filePatterns, disables test and lint when command-line.json declares no bulk or phased command of that name, and retracts a former project. It rewrites a file only when a member it owns changes.

In delegate mode, putnami validate compares each project's putnami.json with rush.json and the project manifests, writes nothing, and fails with rush.sync_stale when a sync would change one. In import mode Putnami owns the graph, and the check passes.

Each task compares rush --version with the rushVersion of rush.json, then runs at the workspace root rush build --to <package>, or rush test or rush lint --to <package>. Each task depends only on its project's graph step, which runs no rush. Putnami's cache is off for every task, and the result records delegatedTo rush. A failing step fails with stacks.step_failed.

The test task reads the JUnit and coverage files a project names in its putnami.json, under options.@putnami/rush.tasks.test.reports, into the test and coverage summary. A project that names none passes or fails on the exit code alone, and the sync lists those projects.
In delegate mode, when common/config/rush/build-cache.json is missing or does not set buildCacheEnabled to true, the sync warns once that each delegated task reruns the projects upstream of its own.

The sync writes nothing it cannot map. It lists, with the reason, each command-line.json bulk or phased command other than build, test and lint, and in import mode each project script other than build, test and lint; those keep running through Rush.

The manifest passes the stack core's conformance kit: its markers are the profile's, it lists the rush:build, rush:test and rush:lint selectors, each command runs the graph step, which depends on the graph step upstream, then its task, which depends on its own graph step alone, and every task, the graph task included, sets cache.enabled to false.

In import mode, the sync adds exports {".": "./src/index.ts"} to a project's package.json that declares no exports, whose main or types names a file outside src/, and that holds src/index.ts, and writes tsconfig.json extending the workspace root's tsconfig.json where a project has none. It keeps every other byte of package.json, lists each file it writes, and a dry sync shows their diffs.
